tasks.description: F633, measured on the testbed with a plain-session baseline and a blind A/B review: P5.3's text said src is set when the card ENTERS the viewport; the executor shipped `rootMargin: "200px 0px"`, said so, and renamed its test to 'once the card is near the viewport'; the phase reviewer's intentCheck answered `matches` on the basis of the executor's restatement. The blind pass also found two med defects the phase review missed. (1) The intent check QUOTES THE TASK TEXT and compares the diff and the tests against it - never against the outcome text or the test titles; a restatement whose scope differs from the task text is itself a finding, quoting both. (2) The reviewer brief puts the task text first and the executor's return last, labelled as the claim under review. (3) The drive diffs `tests.add` against the test names the return files, mechanically, and a declared case with no filed counterpart is a finding before any reviewer runs. Red-first: a fixture where the task says 'enters' and the return says 'near' with a 200px margin must answer `diverges` and quote both; a declared tests.add case missing from the return is named by the drive. (4) Measured on the testbed with the SAME model (plain Sonnet vs the plugin's Sonnet executors, blind A/B): the plugin's version alone shipped a lazy-load test that cannot fail, an e2e that drives the real server action (a key in env sends real mail), and a test-readiness race (asserting enabled state the SSR HTML already has). So the reviewer brief also asks, per declared test: can it fail on the unfixed code (the red-first block, or say it was never seen red), and does any test reach a real external service or side effect (mail, payment, network) rather than a stub - each a finding with its file:line. Faults: F633. tasks.description: F615 recurred and has a twin, so this is the class, not two instances. CI run 38442950089 (ci/p125 at 125a69b8, windows-latest): test__journal_io sl4 lost a row to 'refused: [Errno 13] Permission denied ... .lock.break' (F615, first seen 2026-10-10, still unfixed), and test_panel_server hr2 had the second of two concurrent POST /api/proposal drops refused ([('first', True), ('second', False)]). The class: on Windows, opening, renaming or replacing a file another process holds is denied, and a writer that reads that denial as a refusal loses the write. One invariant in one place: the lock acquire / breaker / atomic-replace helpers (_locks, and the replace helper the writers share) treat a sharing denial as contention - retried with backoff within the operation's existing deadline - and only a deadline expiry is a refusal. Every concurrent writer (journal append, panel write, manifest write) goes through those helpers; no per-site retry loop. Simulate the denial in tests; never sleep for real beyond a few ms.
